Performers
Chicago Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Frederick Stock (conductor), Walter P. Zimmerman (organ) Documented

The label names orchestra and conductor; DAHR’s Victor-ledger transcription supplies the organist. Elgar is the composer, not a performer on this record.

[2] [3]
Work version
Orchestral version with organ Documented

The label and Victor ledger specify orchestra and organ. The precise performing edition and treatment of every written repeat are not established.

[2] [3]
Recorded
22 December 1926 Documented

DAHR gives this date for issued master CVE-37282 take 3. The July 1927 date is a release-list date, not a competing session date.

[3]
Place
Orchestra Hall, Chicago, Illinois Documented

Named in DAHR’s take table, not inferred from the ensemble’s home city.

[3]
Label
Victrola (Victor Talking Machine Company) Documented

The photographed label explicitly reads Orthophonic Recording: electrical, despite the archive description’s Acoustic technical note.

[2]
Catalogue
6648-B Documented

The other side is Handel’s Largo from Xerxes. Victor’s July 1927 release list identifies the coupling.

[2] [5] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
CVE-37282, take 3; Victor 6648-B Documented

DAHR associates take 3 with issue 6648. Internet Archive’s 6648B matrix field repeats the catalogue-side number rather than identifying the master.

[3] [4] [2]
Transfer
George Blood, L.P.; Jordan Gold, transfer Documented

The item’s scanningcentre and user_transferred fields identify the digitisation facility and transfer worker.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The March 2021 upload is not treated as the transfer date.

[1]
Processing
78-rpm digitisation with four truncated-conical styli; engineer-selected preferred FLAC and MP3 derivative Documented

The item lists 3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil styli but does not identify the preferred file’s stylus or equalisation. Its Acoustic technical note conflicts with the Orthophonic label and CVE electrical master prefix; the recording is identified here as electrical. No new concatenation or audio alteration was made.

[1] [2] [3]
Composition rights
Elgar’s original 1901 march is public domain in ordinary life-plus-70 jurisdictions Inferred, not documented

Elgar died in 1934. No rights are inferred for an unidentified modern edition.

[6] [4] [7]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: Victor 6648 announced for publication on 1 July 1927 Documented

Rule 3. The Talking Machine World, June 1927, p. 157, July record bulletins, Victor list for 1 July, names 6648, Stock, Chicago Symphony Orchestra and Grand Organ. This publication evidence is independent of the December 1926 session; DAHR’s catalogue MARC estimate [1926] is not used as a precise release date. The recording’s 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension. US status is not established. The selected item’s complete metadata, original FLAC and label disclose no NC licence or separate upstream digital audio source; the University of Illinois physical-disc collection is credited by the item.

[5] [2] [3] [1] [7]

Elgar, Pomp and Circumstance March No. 1 — Chicago Symphony Orchestra, Frederick Stock; Walter P. Zimmerman, organ. Orchestra Hall, 22 December 1926. Victrola 6648-B, CVE-37282 take 3, issued July 1927. George Blood, L.P./Internet Archive Great 78 Project transfer, University of Illinois Audio Archive collection. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US status not established. Rights statement
